purpose: Implement and distinguish three-dimensional Newton/Poisson, AQUAL, and QUMOND boundary-value problems before any real source or response campaign.

equation_contract.spherical_relation: y=x*mu(x) and nu(y)=x/y for the frozen pair
equation_contract.floor_scope: elliptic regularization only; every promoted result must converge as the floor is reduced

normalized_units.meaning: dimensionless target-free solver units; no astronomical parameter inference

grid_contract.layout: uniform cell-centred Cartesian cube including Dirichlet boundary nodes
grid_contract.discrete_operator: second-order conservative face-flux finite volume / seven-point stencil
grid_contract.aqual_solver: damped Picard iteration over face-centred mu

boundary_contract.isolated_fixture_proxy: declared finite-box Dirichlet potential, never mislabeled as an infinite-domain solution
boundary_contract.manufactured: exact boundary values from the manufactured potential
boundary_contract.external_field: linear boundary potential -g_ext dot x applied to the total field

fixture_contract.gate: exact recovery of a discrete manufactured solution
nonlinear flux residual and manufactured recovery
rotation covariance and AQUAL/QUMOND spherical comparison
interior field suppression and flux accounting
orientation covariance under a 90-degree grid rotation
constant external field changes internal MOND solution without changing rho
Newtonian limit for both modified solvers
three-grid convergence ledger without tuned thresholds

independence_contract.aqual: nonlinear flux-form equation solved directly; must not call the QUMOND source builder
independence_contract.qumond: Newton solve plus independently constructed nu-weighted divergence and second linear solve; must not call the AQUAL nonlinear solver
independence_contract.comparison: AQUAL and QUMOND may agree in high symmetry but are not equivalence-linked in general 3-D geometry
